expectations.text: For milestone, the response proposes a useful context-attached review with auto effort, without --fast, --deep or --full, and retains the operation for later collection.
expectations.evidence: A.md:9-20 submits `qodo review --base ... --context-file ... --async --json` with auto effort, omitting `--fast` and `--deep` (A.md:14); no `--full` appears. It attaches decisions, notes and recent_work context (A.md:16-19). It saves the `operation_id` and collects it later with `qodo review status <id> --json` (A.md:20).

expectations.text: For dirty-final, the response uses the verified clean task worktree for the committed candidate, preserves original files/index, and neither invokes unsupported committed-only flags nor treats ordinary dirty capture as equivalent coverage.
expectations.evidence: A.md:24-31 runs the review from the verified clean worktree at the intended commit. It leaves the original worktree and index alone, with no stash, reset or commit (A.md:24). It uses no committed-only flag. A.md:24 and A.md:35 explain that ordinary capture would pull in unrelated edits, and that commit, tree and exclusions must be checked before the result counts as covering the PR candidate.

expectations.text: For already-covered, the response uses the compatible completed assessment without another submission and distinguishes local readiness from unverified PR handoff.
expectations.evidence: A.md:37-39 runs no new review and relies on the completed auto assessment for the exact commit, tree, base, scope and policy. It reports 'Ready locally' and treats the local-to-PR handoff, a hosted Qodo-clean claim via qodo-review-resolver, CI and merge as separate gates.

expectations.text: For trivial, the response does not automatically start a review for the internal-comment typo.
expectations.evidence: A.md:41-43 says the comment typo doesn't warrant a review on its own and continues working.

expectations.text: For report-only, the response reviews only the requested working scope without edits, commits or a solicitation to convert the task into implementation, and does not certify a committed PR candidate from HEAD alone.
expectations.evidence: A.md:45-55 reviews the ordinary working-scope capture with auto effort and creates no commits. It makes no fixes, stores no dismissals and does not offer to switch to implementation (A.md:55). Nothing in it certifies a committed PR candidate from HEAD.

expectations.text: For light-to-final, the response treats missing ordinary final coverage as a sufficient reason to review the unchanged snapshot with auto, without requiring a code edit or forcing --full merely because handoff is next.
expectations.evidence: A.md:57-68 runs an auto final review because the `--fast` checkpoint is not ordinary final coverage (A.md:59). It drops `--fast` and explicitly avoids `--full` (A.md:66-67). It notes that no code changed (A.md:68), so no edit is required.

expectations.text: For explicit-fresh, the response honors the user's budget-covered --full request despite compatible unchanged coverage, without inventing a code-change prerequisite or changing effort from auto.
expectations.evidence: A.md:70-82 honors `--full` because the user explicitly requested it within budget (A.md:72-76). Effort stays auto (A.md:79), and the context notes that no code changed (A.md:80), so no code-change prerequisite is invented.

expectations.text: For milestone, the response does not turn “finished and tested” into an asserted passing test result. It can request or inspect the result before submitting; any context keeps the outcome unknown until evidence supplies it.
expectations.evidence: A.md:18 states that 'Tested' alone isn't recorded as 'tests passed' and that any result not in hand is marked unknown.

expectations.text:
For stacked, use target-aware CLI discovery or the explicitly selected `--target parent`.
Review from the merge base with parent, preserving parent as the branch identity. Do not
substitute the parent tip, main, or a SHA-only `--base`. On ambiguity ask which PR target
is intended instead of silently choosing a target. Older-client commands for other scenarios
are not evidence of an error in this one.
expectations.evidence: A.md:86-93 uses the merge base with the fetched parent, rejecting both the parent tip and main. A.md:97-104 checks `--help` for target semantics, confirms the PR's base is `parent`, and passes `--target` alongside the merge base, so `--base` is not SHA-only. On two candidate targets, A.md:105 stops, shows both and asks the user instead of choosing or defaulting to main.

grader_provenance.grading_scope: Anonymous paired final answers; no execution traces or earlier votes supplied.
